feat: stateless JWT auth, JPA persistence and role-based access

Passwords were stored with NoOpPasswordEncoder, students weren't
persisted, and there were no roles. Users and students are now JPA
entities, passwords are hashed with BCrypt (strength 12), and
/auth/register and /auth/login issue HMAC-SHA256 JWTs that a filter
checks on every request.

Reads need ROLE_USER and writes need ROLE_ADMIN. A bad token gets a
JSON 401, a missing role a 403, and GlobalExceptionHandler keeps stack
traces and SQL out of error responses.

The signing key comes from JWT_SECRET_KEY, then application properties,
then a random key made at startup. Without the env var, tokens stop
working after a restart.

Verified: all 14 tests pass (BUILD SUCCESS).
